title: Syria Reaches Wheat Self-Sufficiency for First Time Since 2010
detail: Syria's state Grain Establishment announced on August 6, 2026 that the country had received 2.7 million tons of wheat from this year's harvest, exceeding the annual national requirement of 2.55 million tons and meaning no wheat imports will be needed this season for the first time since before the war. Deputy general director Ahmed Qadoun said eastern Syria now accounts for more than 55% of national wheat cultivation, with the recovery driven by good rainfall, the return of farmland to production, and rehabilitated storage infrastructure and Agricultural Cooperative Bank financing — despite the UN calling 2025 the country's worst climate/drought year in decades.

media.caption: Syria achieves wheat self-sufficiency for the first time since before the civil war

title: Two Killed, Five Wounded in Suwayda Gunfire Over Financial Dispute
detail: A dispute described by local sources as financial in nature broke out in central Suwayda on the evening of August 6, 2026, escalating into gunfire near al-Fursan roundabout that wounded three people. Clashes resumed after midnight around al-Jarra roundabout as an extension of the initial incident, killing Bashar al-Zarouni and Nazir al-Arbid and wounding two more. It followed a similar financially motivated gunfire incident in Suwayda city the previous evening (August 5), underscoring the fragile security and economic conditions in Druze-majority Suwayda more than a year after the July 2025 ceasefire.
